results.q: How is commercial spend calculated?
results.text: Total commercial electricity spend: Average price multiplied by sales, expressed in millions of dollars. Unit: $M. Source: Derived from EIA retail sales (price × sales ÷ 100). Caveat: Derived, not reported. Rounding of sales to whole GWh makes it approximate to about 0.01%.

results.q: What metrics do you have?
results.text: Certified metrics: Average commercial electricity price [¢/kWh]; Commercial electricity sales [GWh]; Total commercial electricity spend [$M]; Year-over-year change in commercial price [%]; Commercial price premium or discount to the U.S. average [%]; 90th-percentile budget overrun (flat +3% rule) [%]; Recommended contingency for the 2027 budget [%]; 2027 base-case commercial price [¢/kWh]; 2027 high-case commercial price [¢/kWh]; EIA outlook growth in price, 2025 to 2027 [%].

results.q: What does the P90 overrun mean?
results.text: 90th-percentile budget overrun (flat +3% rule): 90th percentile of (actual − budget) ÷ budget over 16 budget years (2010–2025), budget set two years ahead with a flat +3%/yr escalator. Unit: %. Source: Electricity Cost-Risk Study (this author's backtest of EIA data). Caveat: Based on 16 observations per state and includes the 2022–23 price shock. Reported for the 2027 budget year only.
